title: Custom Aggregate and Window Functions
learning_outcomes: Describe the main purpose and behavior of custom aggregate and window functions.
Apply a small SQLite example involving defining aggregate functions and verify the result.
Identify one failure mode, compatibility constraint, or data-integrity concern related to this topic.

content.intro: This lesson covers custom aggregate and window functions as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.
content.why_it_matters: Window functions preserve individual rows while calculating across related rows.

items.title: Defining aggregate functions
items.text: Aggregate functions summarize groups. WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups. Remember that aggregates generally skip NULL inputs and verify how COUNT(*) differs from COUNT(column).

content_blocks.title: Example: Custom Aggregate and Window Functions
content_blocks.code:
WITH scores(name, points) AS (VALUES ('Ari', 8), ('Bea', 10))
SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY points DESC) FROM scores;
